p:ABW: The Central Bank of Aruba, created in 1986, issues the Aruban florin, pegged to the US dollar as of December 2025. Its Central Bank Ordinance of 1991 keeps the bank under the Governor of Aruba and the Minister of Finance. Section 18 has the Governor appoint the president and executive directors from a shortlist of three put up by the Supervisory Board, and suspend or dismiss them by state decree; section 19(3) allows general guidelines for their duties to be set by decree; section 23 gives him the appointment and dismissal of the supervisory directors; section 27(1) has the Government Commissioner supervise the bank under the Minister's instructions. One case is recorded: the General Audit Chamber, reviewing the country's 2001-2004 accounts, found contributions to an earmarked account at the bank for the Fondo Desaroyo Aruba foundation were not accounted for completely, correctly and on time, with 16,898,503 florins paid in by the Netherlands left off the balance sheet. Crane Currency appears as having supplied new banknotes in 2019 on another organisation's client list rather than a contract notice, so that is reported rather than confirmed by the bank. BNP Paribas Asset Management runs a fixed income mandate in US dollars and gives advice, Ernst & Young audits the accounts, and Aruba scores 33 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:BMU: Bermuda's money is the Bermudian dollar, issued by the Bermuda Monetary Authority, which is the central bank and held the dollar at a de facto peg to the US dollar as of December 2025. The Bermuda Monetary Authority Act 1969 places it under the finance minister: section 21(2) lets the Minister give it written general directions that appear to him necessary in the public interest, which it shall act in accordance with; section 4(1)(d) has him appoint eleven Board members and section 4E(1) the Chairman, and section 4E(6) lets him end the Chairman's appointment if satisfied he is unable or unfit to discharge his functions. Independence written into law is almost absent, 0.06 of 1 and second from last of 191 places, with no reform since 1970. No documented case at the bank was found, which does not prove none happened. One career move is recorded: Cheryl-Ann Lister, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer from 1999 through 2006, was appointed an independent director and audit committee member of AXIS Capital Holdings Limited, a Bermuda-based insurance and reinsurance group, in an announcement of 23 September 2008. The Office of the Auditor-General audits the accounts. On 30 October 2024 the Authority announced that its new 2 and 5 dollar notes, printed by De La Rue on polymer, would enter circulation that autumn. Bermuda scores 36 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, with financial secrecy at 71.3 of 100.
p:BRB: The Central Bank of Barbados issues the Barbados dollar and in practice holds it at a fixed rate against the United States dollar. Its founding governor, Sir Courtney Blackman, had been an economist at the Wall Street bank Irving Trust Company from 1968 to 1971 and led the bank from 1972 to 1987 across three terms, also serving as Barbados' alternate governor to the International Monetary Fund until March 1987. Five cases are recorded, all findings by the Auditor General about government money held at the bank. His 2004 report found discrepancies with the Accountant General's records for the government current account between October 2000 and February 2004: unrecorded withdrawals above $1.8 million and unrecorded deposits above $6.8 million. The 2020 report found Treasury accounts unreconciled up to 31 March 2019, eight transfers of loan funds totalling $13.137 million made without the required signed memorandum, and the government's overdraft exceeding its statutory limit of 10 per cent of estimated revenue twice in 2018, each time by $10 million. The 2021 report found a $6,662,541.31 difference between Treasury and bank records for 22 September 2020 left unexplained. In 2017 Finance Minister Chris Sinckler dismissed Governor Delisle Worrell; the stated reason was the board's objection to his reported high-handed manner, some observers believed it was his refusal to keep financing the government with new money, and the Appeals Court upheld the minister's right to dismiss him. Otherwise no government pressure was reported from 2010 to 2018. De La Rue prints the five-dollar polymer note introduced in December 2022, PricewaterhouseCoopers SRL audits the accounts, and Barbados scores 35 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:CHL: Chile's central bank is the Central Bank of Chile, which issues the Chilean peso. It scores 24 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and no government pressure was reported between 2010 and 2018. The Constitutional Convention elected to write a replacement for the 1980 constitution drafted new articles on the bank, and on 5 April 2022 its president Rosanna Costa wrote to the Convention on the Council's behalf. The main objection was the removal provision: one third of the members of Congress could have asked the Supreme Court to remove councillors, which the bank said exposed it to political judgements that would diminish its autonomy. It asked that the power be limited to a majority of councillors or the President of the Republic, and that productive diversification be struck from its objectives as not a monetary task. Voters rejected the draft on 4 September 2022. Two cases are recorded, both still under investigation. On 24 July 2012 three staff allegedly tried to take about 38 million pesos in banknotes being processed for destruction, and a fourth was detained the next day. In March 2022 someone posing as the finance chief of the US firm RVK sent a false invoice for 205,000 dollars from an address one letter off the real one, and the bank paid; it complained to prosecutors and dismissed its accounting management head on 23 June 2022, who sued in December seeking 267 million pesos. Three officials moved in from finance or international lenders, which is not an accusation: Joaquin Vial from BBVA, Mario Marcel from the World Bank, Rodrigo Valdes from BTG Pactual and Barclays Capital. The bank picks and supervises the outside firms running parts of the state's sovereign wealth funds, among them BlackRock, Nomura Asset Management, UBS Asset Management, Mellon Investments Corporation and BNP Paribas Asset Management. Note Printing Australia listed it among its export orders in 2006/07 and KPMG audits the accounts. Its swap line with China, an arrangement to borrow another central bank's currency, was renewed on 23 October 2026 at about 7.5 billion US dollars equivalent for five years.
p:COM: The Central Bank of the Comoros issues the Comorian franc, and France stands behind it. A monetary cooperation agreement signed at Moroni and Paris on 23 November 1979 rests on an unlimited French guarantee of the currency the bank issues. It set the rate at 1 Comorian franc to 0.02 French francs; after a devaluation of 33 percent on 11 January 1994, the rate is now 1 euro to 491.968 Comorian francs. The bank must keep 65 percent of its foreign currency reserves on deposit with the French Treasury. Two governments also fill its board. Under statutes signed in Paris on 22 April 2008 it had at most eight members, half named by the French government and half by the government of the Union of the Comoros, with the Governor named by the President of the Union on the finance minister's proposal. Under statutes in force since March 2025, France names two of the six board members, two of four on the banking supervision committee and two of four on the committee that sets monetary policy and manages reserves. Two cases are recorded, both findings of a parliamentary commission of inquiry into the programme that sold economic citizenship. Reporting in December 2017, it found the programme's account TR0044 at the bank took in payments, including four cheques drawn by Comoro Gulf Holding between March 2009 and April 2010, and that the bank booked money in without knowing the price the passports sold for; it put the shortfall at more than 2,900,000,000 Comorian francs, and the account was closed on 1 September 2015. The same inquiry found that, according to his own collaborators, President Ikililou Dhoinine ordered that from January 2015 the funds no longer be paid into the bank and could not explain what became of them, so it concluded he was suspected of embezzling public money. The notes are printed at the Banque de France. It holds no gold, Mazars Fivoarana audited its 2024 accounts, and it scores 47 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed.
p:CYM: The Cayman Islands Monetary Authority acts as the central bank of the Cayman Islands, and the currency is the Cayman Islands dollar. The Monetary Authority Law (2020 Revision) puts the Authority under the Cabinet: section 33(1) lets the Cabinet give it written general directions that appear necessary in the public interest, which it shall act in accordance with, and under sections 12(1), 11(3), 13(1) and 14(3) the Cabinet appoints the directors, designates the chairperson and deputy chairperson, appoints the managing director and may terminate any director's appointment in the public interest. In June 2015 the Authority said it would commission an internal review of the involvement of local people and financial institutions in the FIFA corruption case, after the Caymanian businessman Jeffrey Webb was arrested in Switzerland on 27 May. The husband of its managing director Cindy Scotland, the former minister Mark Scotland, had worked for the Cayman Islands Football Association under Webb and was with Webb at the arrest; Gloria Glidden, deputy head of the banking division, is the wife of the former minister Cline Glidden, who was also in Switzerland with Webb. The chairman, George McCarthy, said Scotland would remain managing director and that there was no evidence any Cayman bank had done anything wrong. That review is still under investigation. One career move runs the other way, into the authority, and taking a job is not an accusation: its own board page says director Greg Swart was managing member and chief financial officer of Farallon Capital Management LLC, a global alternative asset management firm, from 2002 to 2019, and spent about twelve years at Goldman Sachs before that. A commemorative 70-dollar note introduced on 12 October 2023 was printed by De La Rue and is not part of the circulating series. The Auditor General, Patrick O. Smith, audits the accounts, and the authority scores 38 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:FJI: The Reserve Bank of Fiji, created in 1973, issues the Fijian dollar and, as of December 2025, holds it at a pre-announced rate measured against the United States and Australian dollars. One removal is recorded. In April 2009 government officials removed governor Savenaca Narube and replaced him with deputy governor Sada Reddy, hours before the Fiji dollar was devalued by 20 percent; the new government had come to power the previous week and was led by the army. No official reason was given, and the report notes that Narube had recently warned about the economy and forecast a 0.3 percent contraction for 2009. No documented case at the bank was found, which does not prove none happened. One career move is recorded, which is not an accusation: Inia Naiyaga spent 40 years as a central banker, 25 of them on the bank's executive management team, and retired as deputy governor in May 2014; he had advised the board of SUN Insurance since 2016, became an independent director in April 2018, and was appointed managing director from 6 June after chief executive Lolesh K. Sharma resigned. In 2006 the bank agreed with De La Rue International Limited of the United Kingdom to print a new design series, including a 100-dollar note for the first time, and KPMG audits the accounts. Fiji scores 33 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed; its weakest side is corruption and secrecy, 56 of 100, mainly because the country's laws hide who owns money, at 77.4 of 100 on a financial secrecy measure.
p:HTI: The Bank of the Republic of Haiti, created in 1979, issues the currency HTG, held at a de facto peg to the US dollar as of December 2025; the dollar is also listed as a currency there. One case is recorded. In April 2004 justice minister Bernard Gousse barred Venel Joseph, a former governor of the bank, from leaving the country, naming him among 37 former officials to be kept available for investigations into crimes alleged against the government of ousted president Jean-Bertrand Aristide, and calling the travel ban an insurance policy. What conduct at the bank, if any, was being looked into is not reported, and no charge and no finding followed. The bank has also been called before parliament: the Senate's Economy and Finance commission summoned governor Charles Castel, with Ronald Baudin, Minister of Economy and Finance, to appear on Wednesday 1 June 2011 and answer questions about new taxes of 1.50 US dollars per money transfer and 5 cents a minute on incoming international calls. Government pressure was reported in 0 of 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018. KPMG S.A. and the firm Merove-Pierre - Cabinet d'Experts-Comptables audit the accounts jointly, their report covering the year ended 30 September 2021. Haiti's exposure score is 36 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. Corruption and secrecy around the bank scores 82, with a Corruption Perceptions Index score of 16 of 100 and money-laundering risk of 8.12 of 10, rank 2 of 177 where 1 is riskiest.
p:KOR: South Korea's money is the won, issued by the Bank of Korea, which scores 26 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. One episode of government pressure is recorded. Choi Kyung-hwan became deputy prime minister for the economy and finance minister in July 2014 and pressed publicly for lower rates, saying he had not mentioned the base rate and that the central bank should get the hint. On 14 August 2014 the bank cut its base rate by a quarter point to 2.25 percent, the first move in fifteen months, and cut again to 2.0 percent on 15 October; reporting at the time described both cuts as made under government pressure. Governor Lee Ju-yeol said the decision was his committee's and its independence guaranteed. Two cases are recorded, both ending in conviction. Between 2022 and 2023 a currency-exchange employee at the Daejeon Sejong-Chungnam headquarters broke the rule that older coins leave the vault first, at a coin collector's request, letting 240,000 one-hundred-won coins from 2018 and 2019 go out ahead of 2017 coins; the collector made about 180 million won selling them and gave the employee about 55 million, and the Daejeon District Court imposed two years and six months in prison, a fine and confiscation. Between 2013 and 2015 an employee handling publication sales receipts diverted about 56 million won to a personal account and spent about 12 million won on commemorative banknote sheets with a corporate card; the Seoul Central District Court gave eight months suspended for two years, the money having been repaid. Three officials arrived from outside, which is not an accusation: Hwang Geon-il from the World Bank to the rate-setting Monetary Policy Committee, Rhee Chang-yong from the International Monetary Fund, nominated governor on 23 March 2022, and Lim Ji-won from JP Morgan's Seoul branch, who took office on the committee on 17 May 2018 and sold her remaining 6,486 JP Morgan shares that summer, within the law as it then stood. The notes and coins are made by the state-run Korea Minting and Security Printing Corporation, and the Board of Audit and Inspection audits the accounts alongside an auditor appointed by the President. A newspaper report of 12 February 2025 says all 104.4 tonnes of South Korea's gold, bought between 2011 and 2013, is stored at the Bank of England; that is the paper's own wording, so it is reported rather than confirmed by the bank.
p:MLT: Malta uses the euro, so its interest rates are set by the European Central Bank, in which the Central Bank of Malta takes part. Its own case concerns governor Edward Scicluna, a former finance minister: on 29 May 2024 he pleaded not guilty to fraud over the government's handling of a private hospital contract, the Vitals concession, while he was minister, and the charges remain unproven. He stepped aside in July 2024, deputy governor Alexander Demarco replacing him, after a cabinet meeting appeared to reach a compromise; he had insisted he would not resign, Prime Minister Robert Abela insisted on the presumption of innocence, and he kept his salary, reported at 138,000 euros. He was reinstated in July 2025 after the European Central Bank was consulted and raised no objections. Two further findings sit at the European Central Bank: the European Ombudsman found maladministration over president Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a club of central bankers and private bankers, and recommended in January 2018 that he suspend it, which the bank declined and he did not; and a speech of 18 May 2015 to a private London event was published only the next morning, which the bank put down to an internal procedure error. Malta's own share of the European Central Bank's US dollar pooled reserves is not run from Malta: the Central Bank of Ireland has managed it since 1 January 2008, at Malta's own request. Each euro-area country transferred foreign reserves to the ECB in proportion to its shareholding, and those reserves are managed in a decentralised way by the national central banks on a disclosed agency basis; Malta is the one that handed the job to another country's central bank. Its books have been checked by two firms from outside, KPMG for the financial years 2019 to 2025 and Deloitte Audit Ltd for 2023 to 2027. Malta scores 27 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed.
p:SLB: The Solomon Islands dollar is issued by the Central Bank of Solomon Islands, created in 1976 and holding the currency at a crawling peg to the US dollar as of December 2025, meaning the rate is moved in small steps announced in advance. The Central Bank of Solomon Islands Act 2012 sets out how the government may steer it. Section 37 lets the Minister for Finance, with Cabinet's approval, give the bank written directions where he thinks the coordination of monetary and fiscal policies or the public interest requires it, and those directions must be published in the Gazette and laid before Parliament. Section 41(1) has the Governor appointed by the Governor-General on Cabinet's recommendation, and section 41(3) the other directors by the Minister after consulting the Governor. Section 44 protects them in office: they may be removed before their term ends only for permanent incapacity or serious misconduct, and the Governor only on a tribunal's recommendation. A 2023 amendment left all three sections untouched. One case is recorded: a former employee, Bobongi, was convicted on 39 counts of money laundering and two counts of larceny and embezzlement for stealing more than 1.7 million dollars in old banknotes in 2007 to 2009, while the bank was destroying them, and was sentenced to nine years. Note Printing Australia's customer list says it has produced and supplied polymer banknotes to the bank, with no date or value given. Crown Agents Investment Management manages about 95 percent of the bank's allocation of special drawing rights, a reserve asset issued by the International Monetary Fund, and the Auditor General's Office audits the accounts. The country scores 33 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and the bank is near the bottom of 112 places for what it tells the public, at 3 of 15.
p:SLV: El Salvador's central bank is the Central Reserve Bank of El Salvador, and the currency is listed as both the colon and the US dollar. The IMF's 2023 classification puts the country among places with no separate legal tender of their own, using the US dollar as their anchor; legal changes made private acceptance of Bitcoin voluntary and tax payments payable only in US dollars, listed as steps taken before an IMF loan approved on 26 February 2025. One episode with parliament is recorded. In September 2020 Nicolas Martinez, president of the bank, answered a summons from a Legislative Assembly commission investigating the debt the government had taken on during the COVID-19 pandemic and how it was used, and resigned the day after appearing; no reason for the resignation is given. Deputies asked whether the release of banks' liquidity reserve was designed so banks could buy Treasury paper, and he answered that it was an autonomous decision of the banks. One career move is recorded, and it stays within the public sector: Carlos Paredes came to the presidency of the bank from the Autonomous Port Executive Commission, the National Centre for Agricultural and Forestry Technology, the National Council for Science and Technology and the Ministry of Economy. No case at the bank is documented, which does not prove none happened; Reporters Without Borders rates the situation for journalists here as very serious in its 2026 index, so the court reports a case would be found in may not exist or may not be publishable. Written independence from government scores 0.789 of 1, no government pressure was reported from 2010 to 2018, the Corte de Cuentas de la Republica audits the accounts, and El Salvador scores 39 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:SYR: The Central Bank of Syria issues the Syrian pound, which moves within a band of about 5 percent against the US dollar. Basic Monetary Law No. 23 of 2002, issued in Damascus on 17 March 2002 by President Bashar al-Assad, places the bank and its policy-making council under the government. Article 1 has the Monetary and Credit Council work within the general economic directions of the state approved by the Council of Ministers. Article 8(3) has its decisions passed to the Minister of Economy and Foreign Trade, who may suspend for up to seven days any decision he considers contrary to the interest of the state and must refer a continuing disagreement to the Council of Ministers. Article 69 has the Governor appointed, and his service ended, by decree; article 2 puts the Council's non-bank seats, among them assistant ministers and the head of the State Planning Authority, in the gift of a decree; and article 71 has the Minister name the four supervising directors who sit with the Governor on the management committee. Government pressure was reported in 11 of 37 quarters between 2010 and 2018, each time pressing the bank to ease and demanding that it print money. One case runs from 2005 to 2011: a Vienna court found that the Austrian banknote printer OeBS had overcharged the bank by 14 percent on banknote contracts and that the kickback returned to local decision makers. Prosecutors had told the court that former OeBS employees paid bribes to officials at Syrian and Azerbaijani banks in exchange for contracts to print money, an allegation as reported. OeBS managers were convicted in 2014 and again on retrial in 2018, and no Syrian official was named or tried. Syria appoints no private audit firm: article 68(3) of the same law gives the auditing of the bank's records and accounts to the Central Organization for Financial Control, the state's own supreme audit institution. A circulating 500-pound note is printed by Goznak, the Russian state currency works. Syria scores 40 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:TJK: The National Bank of Tajikistan issues the somoni, which it keeps within a band of 2 per cent or less against the US dollar. The Law on the National Bank of Tajikistan, No. 722 of 28 June 2011, signed by President Emomali Rahmon, puts every seat on the bank's Board in the President's hands. Article 74(4) has the Chairman and his deputies appointed and released from office by presidential decree, with the decrees submitted to the lower house of parliament for approval; article 74(3) has the Board's three independent members approved by the President on the Chairman's proposal; and article 74(6) has the President set the salary of the Chairman and his deputies. One case is recorded, as an official finding: in March 2008 the International Monetary Fund's Executive Board found the bank had supplied inaccurate information on the cotton sector, international reserves, net domestic assets and credit policy, reporting reserves of about 450 million US dollars when they were roughly a third of that and concealing that reserves were pledged as collateral for cotton loans; Tajikistan was required to repay 47.4 million US dollars. No government pressure was reported from 2010 to 2018. It has one swap line, an arrangement to borrow another central bank's currency: 3 billion yuan with China, signed on 3 September 2015 to run three years and extendable by agreement, drawn on for 1 million yuan in January 2016; whether it is in force is not known. Its commemorative 100-somoni note, circulated on 30 October 2025, was printed by Giesecke+Devrient of Germany, that note alone and not the regular series. RSM Tajikistan LLC signed the auditor's report on the 2023 statements; the firm holds a licence to audit banks issued by the National Bank itself, so the body being audited also licenses its auditor. Earlier audits were done by Deloitte and by Ernst & Young Ford Rhodes Sidat Hyder. Tajikistan scores 36 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed.
p:TLS: Timor-Leste has its own central bank, the Central Bank of Timor-Leste, created in 2001, but not its own currency: it uses the United States dollar. The International Monetary Fund's 2023 classification lists it among the places with no separate legal tender and the dollar as anchor. One case is recorded. In its report and opinion on the 2019 General State Account, the country's Court of Accounts found that 6.6 million US dollars of European Union direct budget support, held in three bank accounts at the central bank, was not booked as state revenue, so 2019 state revenue was understated by that amount, and that the 2.3 million US dollars spent from those accounts was spent outside the state budget and the General State Account. The same report recorded a closing accounting balance of 4.4 million US dollars against a cash balance at the central bank of 5.2 million. Timor-Leste scores 34 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, more exposed than 63 per cent of the 194 places with a figure. Its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it, 57, with a Corruption Perceptions Index score of 44 of 100 for 2025. The independence the law gives the bank is comparatively strong, 0.777 of 1 and rank 50 of 191. Ernst & Young Audit & Associados - SROC, S.A. audited the 2023 accounts.
p:TON: The National Reserve Bank of Tonga issues the pa'anga, which follows a crawling peg or a band of 1 per cent or less against the US dollar. The National Reserve Bank of Tonga Act, Chapter 16.12 in its 2020 revised edition, sets out how the government may steer it. Section 10(1) has the Minister, with Cabinet's consent, appoint five directors and the Chairman and Deputy Chairman, and section 11(1) has the Governor appointed by Cabinet on the Minister's recommendation. Section 50(1) lets the Minister, with Cabinet's consent, issue the bank written directives, and section 50(4) requires him to put any disagreement with the Board over a policy it has determined to Cabinet, which then determines the policy the bank adopts. The Governor is protected in office: under section 11(3) he may be removed by Cabinet, on the Minister's recommendation made at the Board's request, only for permanent incapacity, serious misconduct or failure to perform his duties. Two cases are documented. In 2024 and 2025 Tonga's Anti-Corruption Commissioner sued the bank and its directors, alleging that a 2024 staff payment, for example $6,600 to each of 73 staff, was an unlawful bonus linked to record profit; the board had described it as a one-off anniversary payout, and on 20 November 2025 the Court of Appeal dismissed the proceedings, finding no reasonable cause of action. Between 2017 and 2019 a Senior Exchange Control Officer forged a Government bond to support another person's New Zealand visa application and asked for $2,500 pa'anga; she pleaded guilty, her employment was terminated, and on 21 May 2019 the Supreme Court of Tonga gave her a two-year sentence, fully suspended, and ordered $800 compensation. Coopers & Lybrand audited the 1993 accounts, and De La Rue printed the 100-pa'anga note in the family introduced on 4 December 2023. Tonga scores 33 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:MRT: The Central Bank of Mauritania issues Mauritania's money, the ouguiya, and scores 30 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed; its weakest side is corruption in the country and money-laundering risk in its banks. Central Banking reported on 30 July 2004 that President Maaouiya Ould Taya had sacked the chairman of the bank, the day after sacking his whole economic team, and that Zeine Ould Zeidane, formerly an adviser to the president, was installed in his place. The report names neither the sacked chairman nor any reason and gives no calendar date, saying only that it happened on the Monday. It rests on a single account relayed from IRIN, so it is reported rather than confirmed. One case is recorded, from 2020 and 2021, and it is still an investigation. In July 2020 police working under the Nouakchott-Ouest prosecutor arrested six people, one of them a bank employee, over foreign currency taken from the central bank; early reports put the amount at about 1 million US dollars and later reports at 2.4 million, plus 500,000 dollars in counterfeit notes. By March 2021 seven people were in pretrial detention, presumed to have taken about 1 million dollars, and supporters held a sit-in demanding a quick trial. No trial or verdict is reported. The governor also signed an agreement with the World Bank treasury for advice, training and help setting up a trading room for managing reserves. On who makes the money the record is thin: an industry body's profile says the 20-ouguiya polymer note launched on 28 November 2021 was made by the Canadian Bank Note Company, Limited, a third-party announcement rather than anything confirmed on the bank's own site. The 50-ouguiya note marking fifty years of the currency, introduced on 18 June 2023, came on three substrates, Durasafe composite by Landqart, paper with sisal by Oberthur and Hybrid by Louisenthal, while its printer is recorded as unknown.
p:UGA: The Bank of Uganda issues the Ugandan shilling, and the Auditor General audits its accounts under section 43 of the Bank of Uganda Act. One case is recorded. A confidential 2018 Auditor General report to parliament said bank managers, including governor Mutebile, acted without guidelines, regulations or policies and may have intentionally neglected aspects of the closure and sale of at least seven commercial banks between 1993 and 2017, including Crane Bank in 2016 and 2017. These are the findings of a report, not court verdicts. Sudhir Ruparelia, dfcu Bank and Nile River Acquisition Company are named in the case, the last two as having received money, favours or contracts from the central bank. Parliament then put the bank through a public inquiry over the same closures. The Auditor General, John Muwanga, presented his special audit to the Speaker of Parliament on 27 August 2018; it had been requested in November 2017 by the chairman of Parliament's Committee on Commissions, Statutory Authorities and State Enterprises, the bank had tried to stop it, and it questioned how the bank spent over 400 billion shillings closing Crane Bank, half of it not recovered. The committee, chaired by Abdu Katuntu, took evidence from the governor, Emmanuel Tumusiime-Mutebile, his deputy Louis Kasekende and other officials from late 2018 into 2019, and on 1 November 2018 Katuntu sent the governor and deputy governor away for arriving without the documents. Mutebile told the committee on 12 November that the seven banks were put under resolution largely because they were insolvent, said he had never delegated his powers to agree the sale of Global Trust Bank to DFCU Bank, and said liquidation reports had been kept from him by junior staff, which raised the question in public of whether he was in charge of his own institution. The committee's report, finalised in February 2019, recommended individual accountability for the officials implicated; demands in Parliament for action against them later stalled. The bank's banknote printing contract is with Oberthur Fiduciaire, signed on 26 July 2018. Northern Trust supplies compliance, performance and risk analysis and a dashboard for watching the outside firms that invest its money, which is analysis and advice rather than management of the money. Uganda scores 34 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:BIH: The convertible mark is issued by the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina under a currency board: marks are put into circulation only against convertible foreign currency the bank holds, at 1.95583 marks to the euro, and its monetary liabilities may never exceed its foreign currency assets. Its law scores 0.899 of 1 for independence, 11th of 155 countries, and no government pressure was reported in the quarters from 2010 to 2018. One case is documented: in 2023 a criminal complaint accused governor Senad Softic of suspected wrongdoing in several matters, including a project to acquire an office building in Pale and a procedure to buy land in Sarajevo. The prosecutor's office said in February 2023 that it had opened a case and was verifying the allegations, which remain unproven, while the bank said examining allegations is not an investigation and that reports of one were untrue. The state has twice acted on the bank. On 25 June 2019 two of the five members of its Governing Board were dismissed by the country's tripartite Presidency, the collective head of state, with the reasons unclear. And in April 2025 the Council of Ministers adopted a revised state budget that settled the liability from the Viaduct arbitration out of the bank's profits; the bank suspended the transfer of 244.3 million marks, part of its 412.6 million marks of 2024 net profit, to the Ministry of Finance and Treasury, saying the move would endanger its assets and the country's financial stability. One career move is recorded, and moving between jobs is not wrongdoing: the bank's own page gives Jasmina Selimovic as an independent member of the Supervisory Board of Raiffeisen Bank Bosnia and Herzegovina in 2018, president of the board of the Sarajevo Canton Institute of Health Insurance since 2021, and appointed to the bank's Governing Board on 3 January 2024. Who prints the mark rests on an encyclopaedia entry rather than anything the bank publishes: it reports that Oberthur Fiduciaire prints every denomination except the 200-mark note, and that OeBS was chosen after an international tender to print the 200. Grant Thornton d.o.o. Banja Luka audited the 2016 accounts. The bank is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements, and it has joined the World Bank Treasury's Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership, which offers advice, training and asset management, the announcement stating the membership rather than which services the bank takes. It scores 39 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed.
p:IRQ: The Central Bank of Iraq issues the dinar and keeps it within a band of 2 percent or less against the US dollar. It scores 36 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and 0.733 of 1 for the independence written into its law, where 1 means the bank holds the power and 0 the government. In 2012 Iraq's Board of Supreme Audit examined the bank's daily auctions of dollars to banks and found that most transactions rested on fraudulent paperwork; the country's top auditor told US officials that up to 800 million dollars a week was leaving Iraq illegally, as reported by the US Special Inspector General for Iraq Reconstruction. In October 2012 the cabinet removed governor Sinan al-Shabibi and named a successor while a parliamentary committee was examining possible manipulation of the dinar and charging that bank officials were abusing the dollar sales. A committee member said arrest warrants had been issued for 30 people, including al-Shabibi and his deputy Mudher Saleh, and the Supreme Judicial Council confirmed warrants without saying what the charges were. The integrity committee's chairman said the inquiry was not about money but about procedures, while a member of the finance committee called it a political decision and not professional; al-Shabibi's defence called the case politically motivated. No court outcome was ever found, so nothing was proven; he died on 8 January 2022, and the bank mourned him as a distinguished former governor. It holds 175.6 tonnes of gold, and the Board of Supreme Audit audits its accounts. Who prints the dinar rests on an encyclopaedia entry rather than anything the bank publishes: it says the 2003 series, still the basis of circulating notes, was printed by De La Rue.
p:ISR: Israel's money is the shekel and its central bank is the Bank of Israel. It scores 26 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and no government pressure was reported between 2010 and 2018. Ministerial pressure came later. Through 2025 finance minister Bezalel Smotrich publicly pressed governor Amir Yaron to cut interest rates, calling the February decision to hold the rate at 4 percent wrong and asking him to reverse it, and on 4 September 2025 telling business leaders that if the governor would not lower rates he would lower taxes instead. The bank answered that the governor and the Monetary Committee decide on professional grounds alone; Smotrich said in the same remarks that the bank's independence was critical and that he had no intention of interfering. On 29 April 2002 State Comptroller Eliezer Goldberg reported that former governor Jacob Frenkel unlawfully received hundreds of thousands of shekels when he resigned, approved by a senior official who reported to him; Goldberg did not say whether the money should be demanded back. On 3 February 2009 Globes reported that a draft comptroller report alleged flaws in the bank's supervision of Bank Hapoalim's sub-prime investments, on which Hapoalim wrote off 1.5 billion dollars; the bank said it had responses to all the points, and this is unproven. A comptroller report on 17 October 2012 found supervision of the bank's reserves dealing deficient as those reserves grew from 28 to 75 billion dollars, with no control over the receipt of bids; the bank said some issues had been corrected during the audit. Four officials have moved between the bank and private finance or international lenders. Frenkel, governor from 1991 to 2000, came from the International Monetary Fund and afterwards chaired Merrill Lynch International, became a vice-chairman of AIG and chaired JPMorgan Chase International. Stanley Fischer, governor from 2005 to 2013, came from the World Bank, the IMF and Citigroup. Karnit Flug joined the IMF in 1984 and the bank's research department in 1988, becoming deputy governor in July 2011 and governor on 13 November 2013. BlackRock is an outside manager for the equities and corporate parts of the bank's portfolio and helped build its strategic asset allocation methodology. Ernst & Young's Israeli firm, Kost Forer Gabbay & Kasierer, audits the accounts. Who prints the shekel rests on an encyclopaedia entry rather than anything the bank publishes: it names Orell Fussli Security Printing of Switzerland, while the bank's own currency pages name no printer.
